title: Cross-architecture numerical divergence in long-stream RNNT decoding
observation: The algebraically equivalent affine-LayerNorm fusion changes final tensors by only about 1e-7, yet stock gfx1201 follows a deterministic long-stream transcript trajectory with 42.07% normalized word-token error while the fused gfx1201 trajectory matches gfx1100 at 37.39%.
questions: Where do gfx1100 and stock gfx1201 first diverge?
Does divergence begin in encoder activations or decoder/token selection?
How does F32, F16, or Q8_0 change the trajectory?
Does fusion merely perturb gfx1201 toward the gfx1100 trajectory?
Does deterministic gfx1201 reproduce the same divergent trajectory across cold starts and builds?
suspected_mechanism: small cross-architecture floating-point differences cross sensitive RNNT token-selection boundaries and compound autoregressively
cheapest_falsifier: capture layer/checkpoint hashes and decoder logits around the first stock gfx1100/gfx1201 token divergence on dots-full.wav
correctness_risk: high for numerically close optimizations because transcript identity is not implied by small tensor error
